answer: Because the sparrow liability is entered in the beacon ledger at admission, the basalt audit makes public the shared exposure and internal sponsorship is self-defeating. A farm must as a result place its own capital behind every alias it sponsors, which is the same as paying the bond twice for each key it runs. A sponsor carries 51% of any slash its member incurs, so vouching is a financial position rather than a courtesy. That is 13 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
